item.description: The proposed ordinance establishes the City’s authority to opt in to Level 2 background screening in accordance with Florida Statute 166.0442. Adoption of the ordinance is necessary for the City to utilize Level 2 background checks for positions of employment or appointment which the City determines is critical to security or public safety. This also includes any private contractor, vendor, repair person, or delivery person who has access to any public facility or publicly operated facility that the City determines critical to security or public safety. This ordinance will support the City’s effort to maintain appropriate background screening standards.

This ordinance amends Section 19-63 of the City of Flagler Beach Code of Ordinances to clarify and update the City’s golf cart registration requirements. The ordinance establishes that initial registration and annual renewal fees will be set by the City’s adopted Fee Schedule, clarifies that registrations are valid from January 1 through December 31, and establishes the requirements for renewing or obtaining a new registration when a registration is not timely renewed. item.description: To meet the mandates of City ordinances and Florida State Statutes with respect to stray animals, animal bites and animal investigations, the City is required to provide secured facilities to be utilized for the holding and quarantine of these animals. Because the City does not have the facilities, staff, training or capacity to meet needed service requirements, we have contracted with the Flagler Humane Society to provide these services. item.description: The City of Flagler Beach currently relies on a single water transmission main crossing the Intracoastal Waterway at North 3rd Street. This configuration presents a significant operational vulnerability: any failure, emergency repair, or unplanned outage at the crossing would disrupt potable water service and fire protection capacity for the barrier island. To address this risk, the City has planned construction of a redundant water main crossing at North 10th Street. The upland portion of the redundant main along Lambert Avenue has already been designed, and construction bids have been received.
